science.title: Partial lunar eclipse visible in Swift Current Thursday night
science.description: Southwest residents can break out their telescopes or plan a trip to an area without light pollution to witness the red glow and cosmic spectacle of a partial lunar eclipse. When to watch According to timeanddate.com, Swift Current will experience the best view of the eclipse at 10:12 p.m. on Thursday, August 27, under a clear dark sky, weather permitting. The moon will begin rising around 7:56 p.m., and the partial eclipse will begin at 8:33 p.m. by beginning to turn red. For Swift Current and the southwest, the moon will be located 132 degrees southeast at an altitude of 18.1 degrees.
